instruction: 评价作者回应在文字层面是否充分处理原关切。先拆解要求，再核每项回应是否直接、完整、具体且有适当理由。采用sufficient / partially_sufficient / insufficient / insufficient_evidence。合理拒绝或解释资料无法补收可以充分；接受建议、礼貌用语或字数本身不加分。不要机械认同评审的错误前提。只提供回应，不提供修订稿；不可声称实际修改已验证。revision_verification必须为not_assessed。不得联网寻找原论文或参考答案。引证只能使用本题输入中的精确文字。

input.comment_text:
The design is retrospective and depends on questionnaires for PTSD, growth, and virtues. Although such questionnaires can be reliable and informative, it is less clear that they are valid for what they purport to measure. Many PTSD researchers have doubts about what PTSD self-reports capture. In addition, for readers to understand what is measured by the virtues questionnaire, we would need a fuller description. The VIA has a very doubtful structure and content but less is known about the validity of the Chinese Virtues Questionnaire, so I would need to review copies of all the questionnaires in English before making a recommendation.

I suspect that the findings and conclusions are justified, but as I mentioned I would prefer to see the questionnaires before making further comments. This is important work that should be continued. I just don't have confidence that I know what you have measured without seeing the questionnaires themselves. I cannot really make a specific recommendation yet without that.
input.response_text: We included English version of used questionnaires as supplementary documents, which can help researchers clearly understand what they are measured. Furthermore, in the revision, we also add item samples for Chinese Virtues Questionnaire (Page 6, Line 15-16): Item samples include “I can accept love from others” (Relationship), “I like to think of new ways to do things” (Vitality), and “I control my emotions” (Conscientiousness).
